title: Inspect Weaver configuration, readiness, and maintenance
summary: Interpret Weaver reading configuration, private state, live readiness, owned admission holds, release selection, and installation recovery without authoring a document.
use_when: Weaver reading configuration, state compatibility, readiness, maintenance drain, release selection, or installation guarantees must be understood.
do_not_use_when: A narrative must be authored or revised, or Annals source intake, Nucleus authentication, scheduling, or retired Weaver workflows must be operated.
outcome: Weaver configuration, state, readiness, maintenance, or release evidence is interpreted through its supported current-user interfaces.
effects: Configuration initialization creates schema 1 only in absent or empty state and atomically stores the Annals reader selection. Existing documents remain unchanged.
Run-owned maintenance holds block new authoring and preserve exact resume; release removes only the selected owner. Readiness and release inspection create no model job or narrative.

The maintained product command selects local program and provider files and writes configuration and state under ordinary admission and the runner lock. Uninstall detaches owned selectors and retains private state.
authority: Weaver owns its reading configuration, private document and recovery state, runner exclusion, deployment admission, and program/provider release selection.
Annals owns source identity and accepted text. Nucleus owns execution, authentication, job inventory, and its separate retained state. Cell owns shared deployment coordination.
success: Ordinary doctor and maintenance operations report readiness and drain. Installation performs setup without artifact-integrity, state-integrity, or operational-readiness checks; its inspection reads release metadata.
failure_and_recovery: Unsupported state, unavailable job inventory, foreign selectors and unproved drain stop the operation. Do not edit SQLite or delete a hold.

A failed deployment retains completed file, configuration and state changes. The executor performs no automatic retry, rollback or product recovery. An interrupted command has unknown effects; inspect current product state and complete authorized recovery separately from acknowledgement of executor admission. Preserve separately acquired holds.
privacy: Requests, documents, and pending tool replies are private. Nucleus may retain full source reads. Weaver clears acknowledged replies and keeps documents and invocation records without automatic pruning.

CLI usage recording requires a nonempty CODEX_THREAD_ID. Chancery records command identity, time, and thread ID in its private journal. Arguments, output, outcomes, and internal product calls are excluded. Recording errors do not change command results.
does_not_authorize: Narrative authoring, source mutation, Nucleus credential changes, publication, email, automatic retry, deletion of private state, or release of another owner's hold.

consumers.statement: The current local user, authorized Cell deployment coordinator, and read-only status consumers may use the supported local surfaces within their own authority.

preconditions.statement: State must be absent or supported schema 1. Reading configuration must identify an existing identity-bound Annals decisions library. Live doctor and drain need compatible reachable Nucleus and Annals interfaces.
A held doctor requires CELL_DEPLOYMENT_RUN_ID to match the sole Weaver hold; unheld doctor uses ordinary admission even when an ID is supplied.

inputs.statement: Init accepts an absolute Annals decisions config path and an optional absolute Annals executable. Deployment settings accept only weaver.annals_config and reuse stored configuration when it is omitted on later deployments.
Maintenance selects an exact run owner. Installer inspection reads the current release selection.

outputs.statement: Configuration reports the Annals reader selection. Doctor reports database integrity, source readiness, and required Nucleus capabilities without domain records or model work.

Maintenance reports protocol_version=1, holds, drained and nonterminal_jobs. status-snapshot declares weaver/author on demand and explicitly incomplete. Installer inspection reports selected release metadata.

data_semantics.statement: Drain requires no admitted Weaver process and no nonterminal Weaver Nucleus job. An unavailable inventory remains unknown and cannot prove drain. An incomplete status snapshot does not assert current readiness.
Configuration identifies a reading client and source library, not ownership of that library or a source feed checkpoint. Init does not change existing document content.

identity_and_units.statement: Weaver uses SQLite schema 1 and maintenance protocol 1. A run ID owns one hold. Program and provider selectors identify one immutable release; these identities are independent of document/job identity.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Doctor and maintenance describe state and dependency evidence at invocation. Installation invokes no readiness or release-integrity checks. status-snapshot has incomplete readiness coverage.
No live-read latency, readiness horizon, service availability, or release cadence is promised.

access.statement: The current-user CLI and maintained coordinator are the supported surfaces. weaver.sqlite and config.json are private; files use mode 0600 and state directories use mode 0700.
Direct installer install and recover, foreign selector takeover, direct SQLite integration, a background worker, and a Weaver service or Clockwork binding are unsupported.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Init creates schema 1 only in an absent or empty database and atomically saves reading configuration. Unsupported state is refused. One runner lock excludes concurrent write, write-many, resume and initialization; a batch handles its independent jobs within that lock.
A hold blocks new writes, batches and revisions. Resume can settle an existing exact assignment. Hold and release preserve other owners' holds; unavailable inventory cannot establish drain.

Public program and Chancery selectors follow the selected release. Each selector replacement is atomic; failed deployment retains completed changes. The product command creates no hold and drains no authoring job. The executor performs no automatic application recovery. Uninstall retains private state.

operational_limits.statement: Readiness verification creates no narrative or model job. Weaver has no background worker, schedule or service. There is no automatic pruning or predecessor schema migration.
No retention horizon, database capacity, general recovery latency, or release cadence is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Cell source and active Semantics project are weaver-narrative. The predecessor weaver project is permanently retired; its workflow records are not imported or replaced. Matched program and provider releases preserve schema 1 and immutable historical execution identities.
The installer refuses foreign selectors and unsupported legacy installation formats. Program recovery preserves current Weaver state. Nucleus owns credential recovery.
No future compatibility lifetime or deprecation interval is promised.

reliances.statement: Annals supplies the explicit decisions-library identity and read-only source cursor used for configuration and readiness.
Nucleus supplies live job inventory, compatible execution readiness and its owned maintenance evidence.

Cell prepares artifacts and executes explicit ordered instructions. Weaver owns setup and application recovery. Executor reconciliation and acknowledgement change only execution evidence and admission; no dedicated installed Chancery contract covers the executor.
